title: Arthur Cayley: Collected Mathematical Papers, Draft/Provenance LaTeX Readers and Repair Packets
version: 2026-06-12 accuracy-caveat refresh for draft/provenance Cayley material
description:
Dedicated Arthur Cayley author record for draft/provenance LaTeX readers, repair packets, diagram/table salvage material, TeX sources, and continuation manifests. The current broad Cayley PDFs and TeX are retained for inspection and repair, but they are not accuracy-certified and should not be cited as faithful transcriptions without checking the source scans. Later audit found that portions of the broad volume readers, including some Volume I ranges, can use symbols, wording, or mathematical layout that is not faithful enough to the source.

Current promoted narrow tranche. The current narrow reader-facing restart packet is Cayley_V1_critical_p001_045_v2_20260609.zip, covering Volume I printed pp.1-45 / complete Papers 1-9 with the Paper 6 low-comma/layout correction. Material outside explicitly audited tranches remains draft/provenance or repair-support material.

Status at a glance. [###-------] source-faithful public certification: narrow tranches only; [########--] represented TeX/PDF coverage: broad rendered readers and chunks exist but are suspect; [#########-] provenance: source TeX chunks, repair packets, audit notes, scan-derived diagram/table work, and GitHub mirror preserved, while large raw provenance remains on the main preservation record. OCR, math-OCR, crop, and candidate-TeX outputs are witness layers rather than source authority.

Corrections and contributions. Source comparisons, LaTeX fixes, translation corrections, and reader-facing issue reports can be suggested through the GitHub mirror via issues or pull requests: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.
notes: Dedicated Cayley author DOI. Current broad Cayley volume readers and TeX are retained as draft/provenance and repair material, not as accuracy-certified transcriptions. Use only explicitly audited restart/slice packets as source-checked claims; check important equations, tables, diagrams, and symbols against source scans.
